entries.title: API Reference & DateTime Struct Reference | DTT Lib
entries.content: Skip to main content API Reference struct DateTime pub struct DateTime { pub year: i32, pub month: u8, pub day: u8, pub hour: u8, pub minute: u8, pub second: u8, pub microsecond: u32, pub timestamp: i64, pub iso_8601: String, } Methods DateTime::new() -> DateTime: Instantiates a DateTime with current UTC clock time. DateTime::from_timestamp(i64) -> DateTime: Construct DateTime from Unix epoch seconds. dt.iso_8601() -> &str: Returns ISO 8601 string representation. dt.to_rfc3339() -> String: Returns RFC 3339 formatted string. entries.title: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ): DTT Lib | DTT Lib
entries.content: Skip to main content Frequently Asked Questions Questions? Answers. Expand all How are leap years calculated? DTT Lib follows standard Gregorian calendar rules: a year is a leap year if divisible by 4, unless divisible by 100, unless also divisible by 400. Can I format custom date strings? Yes. DTT Lib provides custom format specifiers for year, month, day, hours, minutes, seconds, and microseconds. Back to the top ↑ ✕ Type to search...

entries.title: Core Features: Sub-Nanosecond Parsing & Timezones | DTT Lib
entries.content: Skip to main content Core Capabilities & Features Performance Zero Heap Allocations All date and time calculations occur directly on the CPU stack with zero heap churn. Compliance Institutional Standard Conformance Strict compliance with ISO 8601, RFC 3339, RFC 2822, and ISO 20022 payment specifications. Timezones IANA Timezone Calculations Effortlessly convert timestamps across New York (EST/EDT), London (GMT/BST), Tokyo (JST), and UTC. Architecture `no_std` Embedded Ready Compatible with bare-metal, embedded microcontrollers, and WebAssembly execution contexts. Back to the top ↑ ✕ Type to search...

entries.title: Getting Started with DTT Lib: Installation & Quickstart | DTT Lib
entries.content: Skip to main content Getting Started with DTT Lib 1. Installation Add dtt to your Cargo.toml: [dependencies] dtt = "0.0.1" 2. Basic Usage use dtt::DateTime; fn main() { // Create new DateTime representing current UTC time let dt = DateTime::new(); println!("ISO 8601: {}", dt.iso_8601); println!("RFC 3339: {}", dt.to_rfc3339()); println!("Unix Timestamp: {}", dt.timestamp); } Back to the top ↑ ✕ Type to search...
